artists.biography: Ireland's Hothouse Flowers made a name for itself during the late '80s and early '90s with a passionate, bombastic fusion of rock & roll with the rootsy sounds of Irish folk and American gospel. The group was founded as a Dublin street-performance act called the Incomparable Benzini Brothers by schoolmates Liam O'Maonlai (vocals, keyboards) and Fiachna O'Broainain (guitar), the former of whom had played in My Bloody Valentine forerunner Congress. After winning the Street Entertainers of the Year award in 1985, the Incomparable Benzini Brothers added bassist Peter O'Toole, saxophonist Leo Barnes, and drummer Jerry Fehily and changed their name to Hothouse Flowers. The group received a glowing write-up in Rolling Stone before even landing a record deal, but that drawback was rectified when U2's Bono saw them performing on a late-night television show. A single on U2's label Mother got Hothouse Flowers signed to PolyGram. Their 1988 debut, People, cruised to the top of the Irish charts and peaked at number two in Britain. Their follow-ups, Home and Songs From the Rain, continued their success, but the band has never been able to break through in America to anything beyond cult status. Hothouse Flowers has been quiet since 1993; several members have guested on other artists' albums.

perplexity.description:
People," released in 2025 on London Records, is a rock album by Hothouse Flowers that showcases the band's early signature sound characterized by energetic and vibey performances with a blend of soulful and introspective elements. The album features standout tracks such as "I'm Sorry" and "Don't Go," noted for their engaging songwriting and occasional humor, contributing to the album's concise yet impactful nature. It includes a mix of upbeat rockers and reflective ballads, with the band's musicianship and emotive vocals at the forefront.

In the context of Hothouse Flowers' discography, "People" represents the foundation of their evolving sound that would expand in subsequent albums like "Home" and "Songs From The Rain," where the band explored more expansive and introspective musical landscapes. The album was part of the band's successful period with London Records, preceding a box set release in 2025 that compiled "People" alongside other key albums and rare tracks from their London years, underscoring its importance in their catalog. Critical reception acknowledges the album's energetic playing and songwriting, though some reviews suggest it falls slightly short of the band's later, more polished works. Commercially, it contributed to establishing Hothouse Flowers' reputation in the UK and Ireland, where their early albums achieved top chart positions.
